Topics · One God, one message

If faiths share so much, why do people fight?

The Quran puts one source behind the traditions' likeness, and the fighting after knowledge, out of rivalry.

Part 1 of 4

﴿شَرَعَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلدِّينِ مَا وَصَّىٰ بِهِۦ نُوحًا وَٱلَّذِىٓ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا وَصَّيْنَا بِهِۦٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰٓ ۖ أَنْ أَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا۟ فِيهِ ۚ كَبُرَ عَلَى ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ مَا تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَيْهِ ۚ ٱللَّهُ يَجْتَبِىٓ إِلَيْهِ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِىٓ إِلَيْهِ مَن يُنِيبُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], and what We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus - to establish the religion and not be divided therein. Difficult for those who associate others with Allāh is that to which you invite them. Allāh chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him].

Quran · Ash-Shura 42:13

Make the list yourself. Honesty. Care for the weak. Some limit on taking what is not yours. Gratitude. A sense that you are answerable, and that something greater than us is not to be treated as a thing. Almost every tradition has it, across oceans and centuries. The verse offers an explanation for that likeness: the same religion was set out for Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and, last, the one who brought this book, with one instruction: hold it up, and do not split over it.

A question for you

What would you put first on the list of what traditions share?

If you sayHonesty and kindness
ThenIt is the part almost no one disputes. The verse says the likeness goes further than manners, to what is enjoined about the religion itself.
If you sayHumility before something greater
ThenMany traditions put it at the centre. The verse is about the religion enjoined, and leaves it to you to say what you think lies at its core.
If you sayBeing answerable for what we do
ThenA widely shared idea, and one of the strongest. It also bears on the question of why division matters, which the next part takes up.
If you sayI do not think there is a shared core
ThenA real position, and careful comparison has found large differences too. The notes on this Step set out the strongest reply on each side.

Part 2 of 4

﴿وَمَا تَفَرَّقُوٓا۟ إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلْعِلْمُ بَغْيًۢا بَيْنَهُمْ ۚ وَلَوْلَا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى لَّقُضِىَ بَيْنَهُمْ ۚ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُورِثُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ لَفِى شَكٍّ مِّنْهُ مُرِيبٍ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And if not for a word[1413] that preceded from your Lord [postponing the penalty] until a specified time, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, those who were granted inheritance of the Scripture after them are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt.

Translator's notes

[1413] Decree. See footnote to 10:19.

Quran · Ash-Shura 42:14

Translation

for you are still fleshly. For insofar as there is jealousy, strife, and factions among you, aren’t you fleshly, and don’t you walk in the ways of men?

Original · Ancient Greek

ἔτι γὰρ σαρκικοί ἐστε. ὅπου γὰρ ἐν ὑμῖν ζῆλος καὶ ἔρις, οὐχὶ σαρκικοί ἐστε καὶ κατὰ ἄνθρωπον περιπατεῖτε;

1 Corinthians · 3:3

World English Bible

If the likeness is real, why the fighting? The verse gives a cause, and it is not ignorance: they split only after the knowledge came to them, out of rivalry among themselves. People wanting to be the ones. This can be checked. Look at where the fights are sharpest: between neighbours, between near cousins, over who is the true heir. In each case ask who stood to gain: standing, followers, land, the feeling of being right.

A question for you

When you last won an argument about religion, what did you feel?

If you sayRelief
ThenRelief often means an argument was carrying more than its topic. It is worth asking what else was riding on it.
If you sayPride
ThenThat is the feeling the verse points to. It is common, and of the four the easiest to see in yourself once you look.
If you saySadness
ThenPerhaps because winning cost something, or because the other person was left worse off. That sadness is a good guide to what matters to you.
If you sayI avoid those arguments
ThenMany do, and it keeps the peace. The verse is about rivalry, and staying out of it is one honest response.

Part 3 of 4

﴿قُلْ يَـٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ تَعَالَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ كَلِمَةٍ سَوَآءٍۭ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ أَلَّا نَعْبُدَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَلَا نُشْرِكَ بِهِۦ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا يَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُنَا بَعْضًا أَرْبَابًا مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ فَإِن تَوَلَّوْا۟ فَقُولُوا۟ ٱشْهَدُوا۟ بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you - that we will not worship except Allāh and not associate anything with Him and not take one another as lords instead of Allāh."[128] But if they turn away, then say, "Bear witness that we are Muslims [submitting to Him]."

Translator's notes

[128] By obeying another in disobedience to Allāh.

Quran · Aal Imran 3:64

Translation

For then I will purify the lips of the peoples, that they may all call on Yahweh’s name, to serve him shoulder to shoulder.

Original · Hebrew

כִּֽי־אָ֛ז אֶהְפֹּ֥ךְ אֶל־עַמִּ֖ים שָׂפָ֣ה בְרוּרָ֑ה לִקְרֹ֤א כֻלָּם֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה לְעָבְד֖וֹ שְׁכֶ֥ם אֶחָֽד׃

Zephaniah · 3:9

World English Bible

Here is what the book offers as common ground: not 'join us', but 'let us come to a word that is level between us and you'. That we worship only God, that we treat nothing as His partner, and that none of us takes other people as lords besides God. Notice the last clause. It applies to everyone, including the people speaking. It puts the speaker under the same rule.

A question for you

Could you stand on that word, whatever your starting point?

If you sayYes, in the main
ThenThen you hold a good deal of common ground with a lot of people. The next part shows where the verses say differences still remain.
If you sayOnly if I knew what 'God' meant here
ThenA fair condition, and where much of the real disagreement sits. Later questions in this series take the meaning of the word up.
If you sayNot without seeing who gets to define it
ThenA sharp worry, and the third clause answers it from the other side: no one takes another person as lord. Notice that it binds the one who is inviting too.

Part 4 of 4

﴿وَأَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ بِٱلْحَقِّ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ وَمُهَيْمِنًا عَلَيْهِ ۖ فَٱحْكُم بَيْنَهُم بِمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ ۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَآءَهُمْ عَمَّا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلْحَقِّ ۚ لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مِنكُمْ شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهَاجًا ۚ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً وَٰحِدَةً وَلَـٰكِن لِّيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِى مَآ ءَاتَىٰكُمْ ۖ فَٱسْتَبِقُوا۟ ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ ۚ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًا فَيُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We have revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], the Book [i.e., the Qur’ān] in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. So judge between them by what Allāh has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from what has come to you of the truth. To each of you We prescribed a law and a method.[268] Had Allāh willed, He would have made you one nation [united in religion], but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you; so race to [all that is] good.[269] To Allāh is your return all together, and He will [then] inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.

Translator's notes

[268] Prior to this revelation, which supersedes all previous scriptures. [269] i.e., obedience to Allāh according to what He enjoined in the Qur’ān and through the sunnah of His Prophet (ﷺ).

Quran · Al-Ma'idah 5:48

Translation

The fear of Yahweh is clean, enduring forever. Yahweh’s ordinances are true, and righteous altogether. They are more to be desired than gold, yes, than much fine gold, sweeter also than honey and the extract of the honeycomb. Moreover your servant is warned by them. In keeping them there is great reward.

Original · Hebrew

יִרְאַ֤ת יְהוָ֨ה ׀ טְהוֹרָה֮ עוֹמֶ֪דֶת לָ֫עַ֥ד מִֽשְׁפְּטֵי־יְהוָ֥ה אֱמֶ֑ת צָֽדְק֥וּ יַחְדָּֽו׃ הַֽנֶּחֱמָדִ֗ים מִ֭זָּהָב וּמִפַּ֣ז רָ֑ב וּמְתוּקִ֥ים מִ֝דְּבַ֗שׁ וְנֹ֣פֶת צוּפִֽים׃ גַּֽם־עַ֭בְדְּךָ נִזְהָ֣ר בָּהֶ֑ם בְּ֝שָׁמְרָ֗ם עֵ֣קֶב רָֽב׃

the Psalms · 19:9-11

World English Bible

This is the other half, and it keeps the first honest. The verse does not say everything is the same. It says each community was given its own law and way, and that had God willed He would have made one community, but He tests you in what you were given. So race toward what is good. It treats differences of practice as real, and treats how we handle them as the exam: not who wins the argument, but who runs toward good.

A question for you

What would racing to good look like between two groups who disagree?

If you sayWorking side by side on something both care about
ThenA very old answer, and often the one that works. Shared work tends to change what the disagreement feels like.
If you sayListening before replying
ThenA small discipline, and a rare one. It tends to change what the disagreement is about.
If you sayLeaving each other alone
ThenPeace is a form of good, and sometimes the right one. The verse asks for more than that, but it does not forbid it.
If you sayHard to picture
ThenIt often is. That is why the verse treats it as a test, not as a default.

The same in the other books

Translation

That your way may be known on earth, and your salvation among all nations, let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you. Oh let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for you will judge the peoples with equity, and govern the nations on earth. Selah. Let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you.

לָדַ֣עַת בָּאָ֣רֶץ דַּרְכֶּ֑ךָ בְּכָל־גּ֝וֹיִ֗ם יְשׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃ יוֹד֖וּךָ עַמִּ֥ים ׀ אֱלֹהִ֑ים י֝וֹד֗וּךָ עַמִּ֥ים כֻּלָּֽם׃ יִֽשְׂמְח֥וּ וִֽירַנְּנ֗וּ לְאֻ֫מִּ֥ים כִּֽי־תִשְׁפֹּ֣ט עַמִּ֣ים מִישׁ֑וֹר וּלְאֻמִּ֓ים ׀ בָּאָ֖רֶץ תַּנְחֵ֣ם סֶֽלָה׃ יוֹד֖וּךָ עַמִּ֥ים ׀ אֱלֹהִ֑ים י֝וֹד֗וּךָ עַמִּ֥ים כֻּלָּֽם׃

the Psalms · 67:2-5

World English Bible

Translation

Pride only breeds quarrels, but wisdom is with people who take advice.

Original · Hebrew

רַק־בְּ֭זָדוֹן יִתֵּ֣ן מַצָּ֑ה וְאֶת־נ֖וֹעָצִ֣ים חָכְמָֽה׃

Proverbs · 13:10

בְּהִקָּבֵ֣ץ עַמִּ֣ים יַחְדָּ֑ו וּ֝מַמְלָכ֗וֹת לַעֲבֹ֥ד אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

Your reflection

Think of a time you were on the opposite side of an argument from someone you respected. What did you both want underneath it?
